answer: An agent economy can stop identity farming with cold-key countersigned registration. Every new identity must be countersigned by a rarely used cold key, and the ledger caps how many identities one cold key may create per epoch; exceeding the cap leaves an umber stain on that key's public record, visible to everyone. Honest operators rotate keys slowly, while a farmer's keys mirror each other: the same funding trail and the same creation rhythm. Each countersignature is stored as a quartz-clear on-chain receipt, so auditors can trace a whole farm to one cold key and slash its deposit.
